candidate.text: Pulling back is where you rest, long before anything has gone wrong. There is more Earth in your mind than you use, and it settles best alone. You withdraw to think a thing through, or you withdraw so nobody sees you thinking it. The price is company, which drains you faster than it feeds you.

angles.drive: Pulling back is where you rest, long before it is any kind of reaction. Company drains a battery in you that solitude recharges, and the door drifts toward closed on its own schedule. Nothing has to go wrong first. The pulling back is the baseline.
angles.cost_self: Three drafts of a two-line reply sit on your phone, and the phone sits face-down through dinner. Nothing about the message is hard. The withdrawing happens earlier than that, somewhere between thinking a thing and letting anyone watch you think it.
angles.cost_others: People stop hearing from you and assume something happened. Usually nothing did, and that is the part worth noticing: the quiet was never a response to anything. Given no reason at all, your door still drifts toward closed, and someone else always has to knock first.

candidate.text: The conversation you would take back keeps running. Earth is heavy in you, and what a day does not use runs at night. You replay it to find a better sentence, or because putting a thought down is something you never learned. It costs you sleep and the evening you were meant to be in.

angles.drive: Holding a thought long after it stops being useful is your mind’s oldest habit. What enters you does not leave on time: it settles, replays, and files itself under unfinished, permanently. All that replaying feels like processing. Mostly it is wear.
angles.cost_self: It is Thursday night and Tuesday’s conversation is still running, paused at the one sentence you would take back. You have replayed it enough times to know it will not change, and you replay it anyway, because putting a thought down was never something anyone taught you.
angles.cost_others: From the outside you just seem quiet. Inside, a committee has been in session since Tuesday, reviewing one sentence from a conversation everyone else forgot. What people read as calm is often storage, thoughts settling in layers and staying down longer than they ever needed to.

candidate.text: You stay in preparation, and the people waiting pay first. Your mind holds more Earth than it spends, so another pass always looks like care. You hand them the finished version late, or you hand them nothing and call it standards. Nobody can call it failure yet, and nobody gets what they asked for.

angles.drive: Getting ready is where you hide, and it photographs as diligence from every angle. As long as you are still preparing, nobody can grade the real attempt, and part of you has arranged your studying life around that protection. Somewhere the preparing stopped serving the step and started replacing it.
angles.cost_self: Seventeen browser tabs, two saved courses, a notebook full of plans. The project they all point at has not moved in a month, but the researching of it has never gone better. One more book, you tell yourself, and the telling sounds exactly like last time.
angles.cost_others: To everyone watching, you are the responsible one, always studying, always ready. Only you know the math underneath: as long as you are still getting ready, nobody can say you failed. It is a clever shelter, and it keeps out progress as reliably as it keeps out judgment.

candidate.text: Your own standard is the only one you answer to. You hold it because it is right, or you hold it because bending would feel like losing yourself. The price is company that can match you, which is rare.

angles.drive: Letting people in stopped being something you decline and became something you cannot quite locate. Fine, you say, on the day of the diagnosis, the layoff, the breakup. The word has three hundred uses now, and not one of them means fine.
angles.cost_self: On the day of the diagnosis you said fine. Layoff, fine. Breakup, fine. The word has become a door painted to look like a wall, and the people who love you have quietly stopped testing whether it opens.
angles.cost_others: The people close to you have learned to read your weather at a distance, because asking gets them fine. They compare notes about you. They worry in committee, exactly the way you trained them to, and call it respecting your space.

candidate.text: You keep your own counsel, and it passes for freedom. Metal is heavy in you, so the surface holds. You stay quiet because the trouble is yours to carry, or because being carried would mean you were seen. Nobody gets asked when you are in trouble, and you pay by being alone with it.

angles.drive: Your rules outlive the reasons for them, and you enforce them anyway. Gym at six, lunch at noon, lights out at eleven, held through a fever and a friend’s one free evening in town. The structure was built to serve you. Somewhere it quietly reversed.
angles.cost_self: A friend was in town for one evening, the first in three years. Lights out at eleven held anyway, the way it held through the fever, the way it holds through everything. You slept on schedule and lay there knowing exactly what the schedule had cost.
angles.cost_others: People plan around your routine the way they plan around weather, and they stopped asking for exceptions years ago. The discipline earns real respect. What nobody mentions is how rarely you appear in the stories they tell about their best nights.

candidate.text: You compete with the people closest to you. There is more Metal in you than one life spends, and comparison is where it goes. You share a stake and count who gave more, or you keep score quietly and call it fairness. The friend pays in trust, without ever knowing a count was kept.

angles.drive: Winning has stopped checking its methods with you. The shortcut through a colleague’s territory, the information used a half-step past fair, the alliance dropped at the moment of maximum value: each move defensible in isolation, and together a style that people describe with one hand on their wallet.
angles.cost_self: The lead was technically unassigned when you took it, though everyone knew whose relationship had warmed it for a year. The commission cleared. The colleague said nothing, transferred out in the spring, and now runs the region you cannot get meetings in. Accounts settle slowly, and fully.
angles.cost_others: People collaborate with you in armor now: terms written, credit pre-assigned, nothing left ambiguous. The precautions slow everything and offend you slightly. But the stories that mandated them are specific, dated, and told to every newcomer by their second week, as onboarding.
